stance: Crawler discovery and verification are dividing between proprietary infrastructure disclosures and an accelerating IETF standardization effort aimed at anonymous attestation and automated outcome reporting.
adoption_shape: Amazon has reinforced bilateral operational transparency by publishing browser-formatted user agent strings and IP verification lists for Amazonbot, Amzn-SearchBot, and Amzn-User, while technical contributors within the IETF Web Bot Auth Working Group are organizing around multi-tiered protocols to verify behavior without identifying the crawler operator.
new_entrants: Authors McKenna and Suresh entered the IETF Web Bot Auth pipeline with new drafts designed to govern privacy-preserving data collection attestation and formalize how authentication outcomes are reported back to clients.
watch_for: Watch for whether major web operators begin ingesting and acting upon the IETF's standardized verification outcome responses rather than relying solely on manual IP list lookups.
